subject: Renewal: Options to preserve 2026 rates with multi-year prepay

Subject: Options to lock rates for 2027 renewal

Hi Neha,

Hope you're well — FinEx is starting our renewal planning for Jan 2027 and we're trying to avoid the rate increases we've seen in the market. We have 3 quick asks and would appreciate your options: 

1) Can Redwood provide a multi-year prepay that effectively preserves 2026 unit rates for the renewal term?
2) We expect usage to ramp over 12–18 months (initial PoC -> prod). Can you include a ramp credit schedule so we don't overpay early?
3) If we commit multi-year, can you offer a pricing cap for any future model/infra-driven increases?

High level: target committed spend ~$600k-$1.2M ARR depending on structure. Procurement is scanning for: annual prepay vs 24-month prepay vs an escrow/lockbox mechanism to hold funds.

Would love a short proposal by EOW Dec 4 so we can socialize internally. Happy to jump on a 30-min call if helpful.

Hi Ella — great to hear from you and thanks for the clear asks. Attached is a short draft (Redwood_Renewal_Terms_Draft.pdf) with three options that map to your scenarios. Quick summary here and a couple of clarifying questions below.

Option 1 — Annual Prepay (12m):
- Prepay for 12 months of forecasted usage.
- 10% invoice-level discount vs list.
- No long-term price protection beyond the 12 months.

Option 2 — Two-year Prepay (24m) with Ramp Credits (recommended for preserved rates):
- 15% up-front discount on committed spend.
- Ramp credit schedule to offset early underutilization: months 0–6 = 30% credit on unused committed units; months 7–12 = 15%; months 13–24 = 5%.
- Price protection clause: model/infra rate increases capped at +5% annually, otherwise automatic fallback to a compatible model variant.

Option 3 — Lockbox / Escrow-Style Reserve (hybrid):
- Customer deposits funds into an escrow that Redwood draws against as consumption occurs.
- Lower discount (8%) but stronger guarantee of rate hold for 24 months.
- Escrow admin fee and legal setup required.

Clarifying Qs: can you share a 3-month token usage profile and whether you need EU-only residency for the data? That'll determine capacity/region pricing.

Next steps: I can run through the workbook with Ben (pricing) and Priyom (legal) and send back a single-sheet recommended structure by Dec 4. If that timing works, I'll include a DocuSign-ready term sheet and an XLS with the ramp scenarios.

Attached: Redwood_Renewal_Terms_Draft.pdf

Hi Ella — thanks for the note and for giving us time to align internally. Attached is a concise workbook (FinEx_MultiYear_Scenario_v3.xlsx) and a short term sheet. Below are two concrete options you can present to procurement: 

Final Proposal (summary):

Option A — Annual Prepay (12m)
- Commitment: prepay for 12 months of forecasted usage
- Effective discount: 10% off list
- Billing: upfront annual invoice
- Price protection: none after month 12

Option B — Two-Year Prepay (24m) — Redwood Recommended
- Commitment: upfront 24 months of committed spend (amount TBD in workbook)
- Effective discount: 15% off list
- Ramp Credits: months 0–6 = 30% credit on unused committed units; months 7–12 = 15%; months 13–24 = 5% (credits applied as invoice offset or one-time credit)
- Price protection: any model/infra-driven list increases capped at +5% per year; if a required model change materially affects output, automatic fallback to a compatible model variant and crediting mechanism applies.
- Early termination: pro-rated unwind with a 10% unwind fee for early termination in year 1, 5% in year 2.

Option C — Lockbox / Escrow Hybrid
- Deposit into an escrow account; Redwood draws as consumption occurs
- Discount: 8%
- Escrow admin fee and legal setup costs (one-time)

Operational notes and asks:
- Confirm EU data residency requirement so we can pin capacity to an EU-only pool (small premium may apply).
- Please share a 3-month token usage export (CSV) so we can populate the workbook and fix committed amounts.
- Proposed procurement timeline: PO by Dec 20 to lock 2026 rates for Jan 1, 2027 start.

DocuSign-ready term sheet link: https://www.docusign.com/sign?doc=finex-renewal-2027
